environment.competingLoad: Team browser tests finished before capture; unrelated browser processes may remain active. Machine-wide GPU load uncontrolled.

scenario.halfScaleDiagnostics: Chrome only, one run each at 1440×900 CSSpx, resolutionScale0.5 for grain/dots/grid; recorded alongside original-scale results without changing effect defaults.
scenario.params: Effect defaults; element-local and mixed-page light-sweep progress explicitly 0.5. Aurora defaultResolutionScale 0.25; all other standalone scales 1. Four additional element-local cases use the mixed-page dimensions.
scenario.rendering: Real DOM attachments with distinct actual canvas contexts and one shared device. Scheduler paused during capture; public beforeFrame/render calls encode all fields into one shared encoder, submitted once per rAF at fixed index/60s. Every field draws every sample, including grain (normal scheduled rate is 18Hz); this is a conservative all-live upper bound rather than automatic scheduler cadence.
scenario.cpuEncode: First field beforeFrame through final field render; includes CSS polling, frame/parameter buffer writes, input preparation, effect passes and canvas resolves.
scenario.cpuEncodeSubmit: CPU encode plus shared timestamp query resolve and queue submission.
scenario.completion: First field beforeFrame to onSubmittedWorkDone callback after the shared submit; includes CPU encode and callback latency, not pure GPU execution. Queue completion awaited each frame; at most one frame workload is in flight.
scenario.gpu: Optional timestamp-query, automatically requested if available by the existing device session; sum of driver-reported effect and actual canvas resolve pass intervals, not elapsed command-buffer wall time. Backend pass interval sums can exceed queue-completion wall duration; raw pass intervals and completion values are retained separately. Asynchronous query-map settlement occurs outside CPU/completion timings. Unavailable/incomplete timestamps leave GPU gate null.
scenario.memory: Logical target/buffer byte counts, not VRAM. Compilation, first-frame startup and readback excluded from measured frame timings.
scenario.gates: Timestamp p95: Chrome aurora0.3ms, grain0.2ms, dots0.3ms, grid0.2ms, other T1 effects0.5ms; WebKit1.5ms. Mixed page completed-work p95<=4ms. Aurora/grain full viewport and four element-local cases are backlog gates. Other full-viewport cases are informational stress tests with appliesToBacklog=false. Total/effect-only/resolve values are all retained; browsers may quantize timestamps, so small timing differences can be below their timestamp precision.
